gaps.sentence: Three out of four respondents — that is, the ___ — supported the change.
gaps.hint: three out of four = more than half
gaps.explanation: Three out of four is more than half, so 'the majority' is the correct label.

gaps.sentence: Three of the six books were mine; ___ were my sister's.
gaps.hint: the defined remainder of a set of six
gaps.explanation: 'The others' refers to the specific remaining books in the known set of six.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.

gaps.sentence: If you walk instead of driving, you'll spend ___ on petrol.
gaps.explanation: 'Spend less' is the comparative with uncountable money; 'fewer' is for countable nouns.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ of room for improvement in this essay.
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of room' is the fixed pattern; 'a lot of' would need the article 'a', which is not in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: The night bus runs ___ twenty minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Every twenty minutes' expresses regular intervals; 'each twenty minutes' is not used.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my friends knew about the concert, so I went on my own.
gaps.explanation: 'None of my friends' means zero friends; 'no' cannot stand before 'of' and 'nothing' is not a quantifier here.

gaps.sentence: He's lucky: he has ___ good friends he can rely on.
gaps.hint: positive meaning with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'A few' means some — a positive idea — and is used with countable plurals like friends.
